title: Bead Aggregation Assays for the Characterization of Putative Cell Adhesion Molecules
protocol: Split HEK293 cells 1:5 using 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA solution.
Incubate split cells in Growth Media at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until 60 - 80% confluent (2 - 3 days).
Culture cells for each condition in 2 x 100 mm dishes.
Transfect HEK293 cells with plasmid encoding Fc-fusion using Lipofectamine.
Return transfected cells to the incubator for 24 hours.
Preheat Growth Media without Fetal Bovine Serum (-FBS) to 37 °C.
Rinse culture dishes twice with 10 ml of Growth Media -FBS.
Incubate the rinsed dishes in 37 °C incubator for 1 hour.
Rinse cultures one more time with 10 ml of Growth Media -FBS, completing three washes total.
Incubate transfected HEK293 cells at 37 °C without FBS for another 48 hours before collecting media.
Transfer media from each pair of dishes to 50 ml conical tubes.
Spin the conical tubes at 500 x g for 5 minutes to pellet cellular debris.
Filter media through a centrifugal filter using a 30 ml syringe and 0.45 µm syringe filter.
Spin the centrifugal filters at 4,000 x g and 4 °C until volume is approximately 500 µl (approximately 15 minutes).
Repeat filtration and concentration steps until all culture media has been processed.
Add 1.5 µl of Protein G magnetic beads to 1 ml of ice cold Binding Buffer in a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube for each sample.
Place tubes on a magnet and remove buffer.
Immediately add concentrated culture media to the Protein G magnetic beads.
Rotate tubes at 4 °C for 2 hours.
Place tubes on a magnet and remove media.
Wash beads twice with ice cold 1 ml Binding Buffer.
Resuspend beads in 300 µl Binding Buffer.
Split resuspended beads into 2 tubes, 150 µl into each tube.
Add 1.5 µl of 200 mM CaCl2 to one tube for the “calcium” condition.
Add 1.5 µl of 200 mM EDTA to another tube for the “no calcium” condition.
Transfer 100 µl from each condition to a depression well slide.
Collect micrographs using a transmitted light microscope.
Collect images from 5 fields of view for each experiment at each desired time point.
